description:
**Sound:** Constant rustling in the bushes and understory trees day & night. Chirps & clicks only in the day. The leaves here are particularly crunchy.

**Smell:** The air is still and dusty. Dust gets worse around leaf piles which decompose into it. If kicked up too much it can become hard to breathe.

**Color:** Occasional canopy tree with dark green leaves and an occasional amber-leaved tree. Understory rhododendrons have dark green leaves and ground underneath is covered in crunchy leaves.

**Light:** Light cuts through the canopy easily. Under canopy trees is dark green moss.

**Verticality:** An occasional climbable tree.

**Young Amber Fir Trees** — Amber to orange colored leaves. Resin leaks from trunk to tip. They are so prevalent they can be used to climb. Resin heads harden quickly into amber. Young resin heads have hard shells filled with delicious syrupy resin — valuable as alchemical base & restores endurance. Old amber heads glow in the night.

**Young Verdant Fir Trees** — Similar to amber cousins but produce little resin. Die younger. Often hollowed out while living. When blown down they become wildlife habitat.

**Dust Devil Trees** — Short understory trees similar to rhododendron. Leaves decompose slowly causing buildup. When disturbed, leaf piles release massive dust — obscuring and hard to breathe. Dust is highly flammable.

**Hollytrop Bush** — Poisonous berries and long tough thorns that stay sharp after decomposing. Ground near them is thick with natural caltrops. Collectible for personal use.

**Yellow Fern** — Grow under fir trees, very densely and tall under amber trees. Waist-high.

**Fish Caps** — Small brown mushrooms that smell like fish when ripe. Attracts cattlepos which will fight for them. Usable as bait for predators and for taming.

**Leanda's Hair** — Strange lichen that looks like hair. Grows densely on Verdant Firs, never on Amber Firs. Great for making durable cordage or rope.

**Pig Pods** — Strange orchids near Amber Firs that tap resin and excrete it with a powerful hallucinogenic toxin. Pods are just big enough for pygmy hogs. A pod consuming a hog has valuable alchemical elements.
name: Amberwood

description:
**Sound:** The Wetlands are silent day & night — only moving water, and an occasional rustle in brush or splash in the water.

**Smell:** A strong sulfuric smell occasionally finds its way to you here.

**Color:** Dark brown muddy waters with pale green & yellow moss which creates a shelf around waterholes. An occasional dark green willow tree.

**Light:** Bright in the day and in the night. The water is lit up by glowing plant life in the night making it easier to hunt aquatic creatures.

**Willow Trees** — Dominant canopy tree of the wetlands.

**Fairy Light Trees** — Dandelion-like seed packets glow as the wind takes them from the tree. The air sparkles with them in the night when the wind picks up.

**Berry Bushes:** Blueberries, cranberries, & huckleberries.

**Berry Vines:** Blackberries, grapevine, & ginger creeper.

**Man-Eater Moss** — Pale green & yellow squishy thick strands up to a foot long. Easy to slip on. Creates a shelf at the shore of waterholes. Can be hard to get out of the water when this moss is present.

**Cattails**

**Lily Pads**

**Glow Vines** — Grape-size glowing fruits glow only in the night. Sneaking in water at night is harder but hunting aquatic life is much easier.

**Splinter Pods** — Large white pods the size of a human head grow on dead trees & corpses. Extract bones & wood splinters into their structure. If touched they explode like a shrapnel grenade. If ignited the explosion is bigger. Small pods can be harvested as throwable weapons. Extraction is very dangerous.

**Ember Lichen** — Kills trees, consumes them, then sets them on fire so their seed will spread. The oil they produce can be turned into a quickly burning weapon coating.
name: Wetland

description:
**Sound:** Howls, chirps, rattles, & clicks ever present in the day. Dead silent at night — only the wind.

**Smell:** Fresh air with a consistent cool breeze under the tall canopy.

**Color:** Deep dark greens with occasional amber-leaved trees. Green ferns up to your knees on the ground.

**Light:** Large canopy blocks light effectively. Moonlight is not enough to light your path at night.

**Verticality:** Large trees can easily be climbed here.

**Old Amber Firs** — Shadow their younger versions. Amber and resin heads grow larger and glow brighter. Thick wide canopy blots out sunlight. Amber head glow visible in cloudy weather during day.

**Old Verdant Firs** — Monstrous trees with thick dark green canopies. Slightly shorter than amber counterpart. Leanda's Hair grows thicker and longer. Very easy to climb. Often have hovels hidden within. Oldest and thickest could hold a spiral staircase. Sometimes contain old Gnomish homes. Sometimes have entrances into the undergrowth below.

**Pillow Moss** — Thick plushy dark green moss grows almost everywhere. So soft it's a little hard to walk on. Easy to sleep on without a bedroll.

**Banana Fern** — Large yellow ferns as tall as rhododendron trees. Rain, loud sounds, and darkness cause them to roll up. Seed pods are yellow, sweet like bananas, very filling and nutritious.

**Weeping Vines** — Pale green-blue vines hanging from Verdant Firs. More water in aquifer = more dense. Can create vine forests dozens of feet deep. Constantly release water drops creating ponds underneath. An oasis — the whole forest comes to drink.

**Coal Shroom** — Large black mushrooms that look scorched. Grow on Verdant Firs. Hard like wood. Can burn and hold ember for days. Makes starting fires in rain easier.

**Slick Spots** — White lichen that grows in place of pillow moss near weeping vines. Very slippery.
name: Deep Amber

description:
**Sound:** Only the underground river. Occasionally a loud crunch. Sound echoes.

**Smell:** Damp and mildewy with occasional whiff of rotting flesh.

**Color:** Verdant greens in areas with sunstone, black & white plants elsewhere.

**Light:** Patches of sunstone shine only in daytime. Outside those zones, bioluminescent creatures often bright enough to light surroundings.

**Verticality:** Waterfalls and crevasses connect different levels. Trees, bamboo, vines, & long lichens create climbable surfaces everywhere.

Fires will attract a predator every time.

*Needs full species population — see biome template checklist.*
name: Jungle Caverns

description:
**Sound:** Sound does not echo. Clicks of high and low tones as consistent as bird songs fill these caverns.

**Smell:** Air smells & tastes sweet but causes burning sensation in lungs.

**Color:** Drab greys & browns with bright blue & green accents.

**Light:** Spores float through glowing dim blue or green. Cannot be seen with a light source. Do not light their surroundings.

**Verticality:** Mushrooms as large as trees. Lichen vines hang from ceiling. Tunnel is wide, tall, and circular. Water runs through center flowing toward crater center.

Heat source required to rest. Fire will attract a predator AND cause an explosion. Filtration mask required.

*Needs full species population — see biome template checklist.*
name: Fungal Caverns

description:
**Sound:** Creaking and groaning of living roots shifting under the weight of the forest above. Dripping water. Distant scratching. Sound carries strangely — echoes off root walls in unpredictable directions.

**Smell:** Rich damp earth, fungal must, root sap. Occasionally the sharp ammonia of creature dens.

**Color:** Darkness. Where bioluminescent creatures are present, brief flickers of cold light against the warm browns and pale whites of exposed root surfaces. Root bark ranges from pale birch-white on young roots to dark knotted brown on ancient ones.

**Light:** Near total darkness. No sunstone, no glow vines. The only light comes from bioluminescent creatures. A torch illuminates root columns and hanging rootlets creating complex shadows that move as the roots shift.

**Verticality:** Varies dramatically. One story tall under the Wetland — crawling and crouching. Two stories under the Amberwood — walking but claustrophobic. Four stories under the Deep Amber — root cathedrals with dangling rootlets like chandeliers and root trunks thicker than buildings.

The Undergrove is not a geological cave — it is a **biological basement** created by the root architecture of Caldera's trees. The roots grow so deep and so thick that they create structural voids between them. Life fills those voids. The ceiling is not rock — it is root. The walls are root. The columns are root. Everything is alive and slowly moving.

The character changes based on what grows above:

**Under the Wetland** — cramped, waterlogged, one story. Root cellar energy. Water seeps everywhere. Moss Roller aggregation sites. Bog Stalker-treated water pools.

**Under the Amberwood** — two stories, denser root columns from the tightly packed trees above. Gilt Weaver root penetration. Creeping Tide highways between cavern entrances.

**Under the Deep Amber** — four-story root cathedrals. Massive root trunks create pillared halls. Bore Weasel tunnel networks thread through the roots. Moss Roller daytime dormancy sites near weeping vine aquifer connections. Gnomish ruins built into the root architecture.

**Root hovels at tree bases** — natural gaps where major roots spread from the trunk. Some large enough to walk into, others require crawling. Cacklers use these to access their lairs.

**Hollowed tree tops leading down** — Old Verdant Firs with bore holes and natural hollows that connect the canopy all the way down through the trunk into the Undergrove below.

**Burrows straight down** — vertical drops through soil into root voids. Some natural, some dug by wildlife. Easy to fall into if the moss covering them collapses.

**Living Architecture** — the roots shift slowly over years. Passages open and close on long timescales. A route that worked last season may be narrower or blocked. The Undergrove is never static.

**Gnomish Ruins** — the Gnomes built their civilization into the root architecture of the Deep Amber Undergrove. Root-carved halls, sap-sealed chambers, stairways spiraling around major root trunks. Much of it collapsed or repurposed by goblinoids. Exploring these ruins is a major draw for scholars and treasure seekers.

**Cackler Lairs** — the Cackler packs make their dens in the Undergrove, accessible through root hovels at the surface. A Cackler lair encounter in the Undergrove is far more dangerous than meeting them above ground — tight quarters, their territory, and the Matriarch nearby.

**Highway Network** — many surface creatures use the Undergrove to travel between areas without crossing dangerous surface territory. Following a well-worn root tunnel might take you somewhere faster than the surface route — or into something's den.

*Needs unique Undergrove plant species — root-parasitic, darkness-adapted, fungal.*

*Needs unique Undergrove creature species that live here and nowhere else.*

Creatures from other biomes that pass through or shelter in the Undergrove:

* **Moss Rollers** — daytime dormancy aggregations in the Deep Amber Undergrove near aquifer connections

* **Bore Weasels** — tunnel networks thread through roots, using the Undergrove as highways

* **Creeping Tides** — emerge from cavern systems through the Undergrove into the Amberwood at night

* **Cacklers** — lair and nest in the Undergrove, hunt on the surface

* **Stalker Bats** — roost in dry sections during the day
name: Amber Undergrove

description:
**Sound:** Daytime — flapping, clicking, occasional hissing, even deafening. Nighttime — crunching, stomping, and the distinct call of countless cattlepos.

**Smell:** Rot, blood, & ammonia so strong it's hard to breathe.

**Color:** Black crusted blood stains, completely stripped bones often shattered into splinters, black soil with white mushrooms around the walls.

**Light:** No light.

**Verticality:** Some caverns are tall and connect to crevasses linking different levels.

During the day — Stalker bats congregate here in massive numbers.
During the night — Cattlepos congregate here to feast and socialize.

**Guano Soil** — Highly valuable. Even just a sample plus info on how to get there is a massive paycheck.

**White Mushrooms** — Incredible healing properties. Minor wounds can be healed in a flash using tinctures from these.
name: Dry Caverns
